modalLead: Health and the Inbox now read the same way: every filter is a row in a left column with its count beside it, the header stays with you as you scroll, and the rows can be compact or comfortable. Monitors becomes a place of its own rather than a filter. On the dashboard, the quick-action toolbar and its keys stay where they belong, and a tag filter survives a trip into Config, the Inbox or Health.

items.text: Health has a left column, like the Inbox. Every filter is a row there with its count beside it, so the tiles that repeated those counts above the list are gone. Score, the trend, the broken count and the report's age sit above the filters as plain readouts. A filter with nothing in it drops out and comes back when it fills; Broken, Content, Duplicates, Unchecked and All always stay.

All monitors is a place of its own now, not a filter. Opening it swaps the list for the fleet panel — pooled uptime, the worst performers, recent outages — instead of narrowing the list the way Monitored still does. It has its own address, so you can bookmark it and come back to the same screen.

The header stays put while you scroll. Work through, Rot report, the ⋯ menu and the ℹ explainer are reachable from anywhere in a long list rather than only from the top. The trend chart moved into the ⋯ menu, as Healthy over time.

A review session can put a link aside for a month. A link that is broken on purpose — a service off for the winter, a host that only answers from home — had no honest answer: Skip brings it back tomorrow, Delete is not what you meant. Ignore 30d is that answer, and it silences the link everywhere, not only in the session.
Health rows can be compact or comfortable, using the setting the Inbox already reads.
Typing in the search box no longer rebuilds the view behind the cursor, and the arrow keys can step past the first filter again.
Uptime 24h no longer reads 0% no matter what your monitors are doing. It says no data while nothing has been sampled yet, and the trend line is back under the trend figure in the left column.
The replay button for the Health tour works again, and the tour it brings back is the one that matches the rebuilt view.

The inbox has a left column too. The filters moved there with their counts, and This week sits above them as a plain readout — it was the one figure that never had a filter behind it. Snoozed and With note appear only when there is something in them.
The header stays put while you scroll, shrinking to a single bar so Triage is reachable from anywhere in a long list.

On a phone the left column becomes one scrolling line. The figures move up under the title and the ℹ explainer joins the ⋯ menu, so a narrow screen gets the list instead of four rows of controls above it.
The site filter no longer sends the site you picked to analytics. It reports a fixed marker instead.

The quick-action toolbar stays on the dashboard. Add, search, commands, finders, recent, help and fold — and the keys behind them — followed you into Config, the Inbox and Health, where they have nothing to act on. They step aside now, and come back the moment you do.

An active tag filter survives a trip into another view. Opening Config, the Inbox or Health threw it away; the header chip that exists to show a filter in exactly those views has something to show again.
Typing in the filter box no longer makes every widget disappear. The clock, the weather and the rest stay where they are while you filter your bookmarks.

Escape stops throwing away your selection. Dismissing the tag list, the checking picker or the date popover left the twenty rows you had picked intact now — one Escape closes one thing. The checking popover also closes when you click away from it, which it never did.
Long category titles shrink to fit again, and a page with nothing on it no longer wears the previous page's column layout.
Alt+←/→ moves a category on a page you never dragged. The keyboard now writes the same order a drag would have, instead of telling you it moved something and leaving it where it was.
Pressing ? while the finder line is open no longer breaks what you type next, and an empty finder list says so and offers the way to make one instead of offering to save your search as a bookmark.

A theme's dark half wears the same backdrop shape as its light half. 111 of the built-in themes drew a different pattern on each side — a diagonal wireframe on one, a glow from below on the other — while only the colours were meant to change with Quick mode. This changes the look of those 111 dark themes, each now drawn with the shape its light half already had.
